paper.title: Evolution in Mendelian populations (neutral drift) / The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

headline: Wright-Fisher neutral drift (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; fixation prob = p0 (worst |err|=0.009); per-gen mean-H decay ~0.9899 vs 1-1/N=0.9900

verdicts.gate: P1 neutral fixation prob of A equals initial frequency p0 (within +-0.05)
P2 per-gen mean-heterozygosity decay factor in [0.9800, 0.9975] (brackets 1-1/N=0.9900)
P3 neutral drift: E[Delta p]~=0 (per-step martingale) and ensemble mean p(t)~=p0 (no selection bias)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the neutral fixation-prob=p0 and heterozygosity-decay results and would catch an artifact

citations: Wright, S. (1931). Evolution in Mendelian populations. Genetics 16(2):97-159. doi:10.1093/genetics/16.2.97.
Fisher, R.A. (1930). The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection. Oxford: Clarendon Press.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. Analytic anchors: neutral fixation prob = p0; haploid heterozygosity decay factor 1-1/N.
